tutorial_steps.label: Step 1 of 13, Sign in to CEAC
tutorial_steps.heading: Sign in to CEAC
tutorial_steps.instruction: Enter CEAC using the NVC Case Number and Invoice ID from the child's Welcome Letter. Confirm that the required fees show as paid and that the child beneficiary's Form DS-260 has been completed and submitted before preparing civil document uploads.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Sign in with Case Number and Invoice ID
tutorial_steps.caption: Case credentials are found in your NVC Welcome Letter.
tutorial_steps.note: If multiple children are immigrating, ensure you are using the correct NVC Case Number and Invoice ID for this specific child. Each child has an individual case number, DS-260, and civil document portal.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 2 of 13, Confirm IV and AOS fee clearance
tutorial_steps.heading: Confirm all fees are paid or cleared
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Confirm all fees are paid or cleared
tutorial_steps.instruction: Before document submission begins, verify in CEAC that the $325 Immigrant Visa fee is paid for the child. Verify that the $120 Affidavit of Support fee is paid, or that the fee exemption for Form I-864W (Child Citizenship Act) has been cleared by NVC.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: IV fee paid; AOS fee paid or I-864W fee exemption acknowledged
tutorial_steps.caption: If payment was made recently, allow 2-3 business days for clearance. Document upload is unlocked once fees show 'PAID'.
tutorial_steps.note: The $325 IV fee is required per child beneficiary. The $120 AOS fee is billed once per petitioner when cases are processed together, or exempt under INA Section 320.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 3 of 13, Start civil document upload
tutorial_steps.heading: Navigate to the civil documents section
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Navigate to the civil documents section
tutorial_steps.instruction: In CEAC, locate and open the child beneficiary's civil documents upload area. This is where you will attach the child's passport biographic page, birth certificate, NADRA CRC/FRC, photos, police certificates (if 16+), custody/consent records, and parentage evidence.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Begin document submission for child beneficiary
tutorial_steps.caption: Review the checklist generated by CEAC for the child beneficiary before uploading.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 4 of 13, Upload documents to CEAC
tutorial_steps.heading: Upload each document individually
tutorial_steps.instruction: Select and upload each civil document under the correct CEAC document category. Each file must be under 2 MB (or CEAC limit). For Urdu documents (such as Nikah Nama or Union Council certificates), combine the original scan and the certified English translation into a single multi-page PDF.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: PDF or JPG files, under 2 MB each
tutorial_steps.caption: Combine original language documents and their certified English translations into one complete file in order.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 5 of 13, Upload documents one by one
tutorial_steps.heading: Process each upload sequentially
tutorial_steps.instruction: Continue uploading each remaining document under its matching CEAC category. After each upload, confirm that the correct file name and upload status appear before moving to the next document.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: One document at a time, wait for confirmation
tutorial_steps.caption: Review each category carefully so a document is not uploaded under the wrong heading.
tutorial_steps.note: Do not close or refresh the browser while a file is actively uploading.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 6 of 13, Upload all required documents
tutorial_steps.heading: Complete the full civil document set
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Complete the full civil document set
tutorial_steps.instruction: Upload every document listed as required for the child beneficiary in CEAC. The core IR-2 set includes the child's passport biographic page, computerized birth certificate (Union Council or local authority), NADRA CRC / B-Form, 2x2 photos, and police certificate (if 16+; exempt if under 16). Add parents' marriage certificate, stepparent records, adoption decree, or custody/consent NOC where applicable.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Required documents checklist completed
tutorial_steps.caption: Use Rahvana's IR-2 civil document checklist together with the case-specific CEAC document list.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 7 of 13, Document unavailable? Use comments
tutorial_steps.heading: Report missing or unavailable documents
tutorial_steps.instruction: If a required record is genuinely unavailable under Pakistan's civil document rules (for example, if a birth was never registered), use the CEAC unavailable option or comments area. Explain the reason briefly and upload official Certificate of Non-Availability plus secondary evidence (hospital records, school records).
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Use comments to document unavailability
tutorial_steps.caption: Check the Department of State reciprocity schedule for Pakistan before marking a document unavailable.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 8 of 13, Document explanation in comments
tutorial_steps.heading: Document your explanation in comments
tutorial_steps.instruction: When using the comments feature, be clear, concise, and factual. For example: 'Primary birth record unavailable from Union Council due to non-registration at birth. Official Certificate of Non-Availability and secondary hospital/school records uploaded.'
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Explain reason and identify substitute evidence
tutorial_steps.caption: State facts clearly: identify what document is missing, why, and what secondary records are provided.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 9 of 13, Document rejected? Review and correct
tutorial_steps.heading: Review rejection reasons and correct issues
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Review rejection reasons and correct issues
tutorial_steps.instruction: If NVC marks a document as 'Rejected' or 'Invalid Doc', click the Response Note in CEAC. Common reasons include: a birth or marriage certificate that is not the computerized version, missing English translation, illegible or cut-off scans, wrong upload category, or missing custody/NOC consent from non-accompanying parent.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Review rejection reason and resubmit corrected file
tutorial_steps.caption: Follow the specific NVC Response Note rather than assuming the problem is only file size or image quality.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 10 of 13, Re-upload rejected documents
tutorial_steps.heading: Upload the corrected document
tutorial_steps.instruction: After correcting the issue identified by NVC, upload the replacement document under the correct category and submit it again. If the file exceeds 2 MB, compress it without sacrificing legibility. If the scan was blurry or cut off, rescan it in color with all stamps, signatures, and borders clearly visible.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Resubmit corrected document
tutorial_steps.caption: Use Rahvana's Document Vault compression tool if file size is the issue.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 11 of 13, Document accepted
tutorial_steps.heading: Confirmation that document was accepted
tutorial_steps.instruction: When NVC accepts a document, CEAC will display the status as 'Accepted.' This means NVC found no correction necessary for that document at the time of review. Continue resolving all remaining document and financial requirements.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: File is now in case record
tutorial_steps.caption: An Accepted status applies to that document; documentary completion requires the entire case package to be complete.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 12 of 13, Check submission status
tutorial_steps.heading: Verify your overall submission status
tutorial_steps.instruction: After uploading and submitting all civil documents, verify that each item shows the appropriate CEAC status. 'Uploaded' means the file is attached but not yet submitted; 'Submitted' means it is awaiting NVC review; 'Accepted' means NVC approved the document.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Confirm documents are Submitted or Accepted
tutorial_steps.caption: Do not stop at 'Uploaded.' Uploaded files must be submitted for NVC review.

tutorial_steps.label: Step 13 of 13, Case ready for NVC review
tutorial_steps.heading: Your case is ready for NVC processing
tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Your case is ready for NVC processing
tutorial_steps.instruction: Once fees, Form I-864/I-864W package, financial evidence, Form DS-260, and all civil documents have been submitted, NVC can review the complete case. If all requirements are satisfied, NVC issues a Documentary Qualification (DQ) notice and places the case in the queue for interview scheduling at U.S. Embassy Islamabad.
tutorial_steps.ss_desc: Awaiting Documentary Qualification determination
tutorial_steps.caption: Check official NVC Timeframes for current document review dates.
tutorial_steps.note: Documentary qualification does not mean the interview is immediately scheduled. Scheduling depends on U.S. Embassy Islamabad appointment availability.

financial_requirements.disclaimer: Affidavit of Support thresholds are established by the annual HHS Poverty Guidelines and Form I-864 instructions. Children qualifying for automatic citizenship under INA Section 320 are exempt via Form I-864W.
guidance: Child Citizenship Act Exemption (INA Section 320): Biological or legally adopted unmarried children under age 18 who will reside in the United States in the legal and physical custody of their U.S. citizen parent automatically acquire U.S. citizenship upon admission. These children are EXEMPT from Form I-864 and file Form I-864W instead. No minimum income threshold or joint sponsor is required.

Affidavit of Support Fee Exemption: Intending immigrants filing Form I-864W are exempt from paying the $120 Affidavit of Support fee. If CEAC automatically generates an AOS fee invoice for an I-864W-eligible child, submit an inquiry to NVC via their Public Inquiry Form to request the fee be waived before paying.

Stepchildren Require Form I-864: Stepchildren do NOT acquire automatic citizenship under INA Section 320. The U.S. citizen stepparent must submit a standard Form I-864 (or Form I-864EZ if eligible), pay the $120 AOS fee, and meet the 125% poverty guideline.

Adult Children (Ages 18-20) Require Form I-864: Beneficiaries who are 18 or older at admission do NOT qualify for automatic citizenship under INA Section 320. They must be sponsored using Form I-864 (or I-864EZ), pay the $120 AOS fee, and meet the 125% poverty guideline.

Active-Duty Military 100% Exception: Under INA Section 213A(f)(3), if the petitioner is on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces petitioning for their child, the minimum income threshold is 100% of the HHS Poverty Guidelines rather than 125%.

Joint Sponsors and Household Members: For cases requiring Form I-864 (stepchildren and adult children), if the petitioner does not meet the income guideline, they may use a qualified household member (Form I-864A) or a joint sponsor (separate Form I-864). The petitioner must still submit their own Form I-864 regardless of income.

tutorial_steps.instruction: In CEAC, check the Affidavit of Support fee section. tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Confirm payment receipt or exemption acknowledgment

This is where you will upload either Form I-864W with citizenship/custody proof (for exempt children) or Form I-864/I-864EZ with complete financial evidence for the petitioner and any joint sponsors or household members.

tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Select correct document category in CEAC dropdown
tutorial_steps.instruction: CEAC requires you to specify the exact document type for each upload. For an exempt child, select 'I-864W Intending Immigrant Exemption' and supporting citizenship/custody records. For Form I-864, select 'Affidavit of Support (I-864)', 'IRS Tax Transcript / Tax Return', 'W-2', or 'Proof of Domicile' under the appropriate sponsor role.

If filing Form I-864W: upload signed I-864W, petitioner's U.S. passport/citizenship proof, and custody/legitimation evidence. If filing Form I-864: upload signed I-864, the most recent IRS tax transcript or tax return with W-2s, recent pay stubs, employment letter, and any household-member (I-864A) or joint sponsor documents.

tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Confirm all required AOS documents are submitted

tutorial_steps.ss_desc: All required AOS documents marked Submitted

tutorial_steps.screenTitle: Check rejection notes if NVC flags a document

ina_320_required.title: Form I-864W (Intending Immigrant's Affidavit of Support Exemption)
ina_320_required.sub: Exemption claim under Child Citizenship Act of 2000 (INA Section 320)

guide.intro: Under INA Section 320, a child who will automatically acquire U.S. citizenship upon admission is exempt from Form I-864 and submits Form I-864W instead.

sections.title: Who Qualifies
sections.body:
The child qualifies for the INA Section 320 exemption if:
  • At least one parent is a U.S. citizen by birth or naturalization.
  • The child is under 18 years of age at the time of admission to the U.S.
  • The child is unmarried.
  • The child will reside in the United States in the legal and physical custody of the U.S. citizen parent.

sections.title: Signing Rules by Age
sections.body: For children under 16, the U.S. citizen parent signs Form I-864W on the child's behalf. Children aged 16 or 17 may personally sign Form I-864W with parent assistance, or the parent signs as parent/guardian. Children age 18 and older do not qualify for INA Section 320 and must submit Form I-864.

sections.title: No Financial Threshold or Joint Sponsor
sections.body: Form I-864W completely waives the 125% HHS Poverty Guidelines requirement. No IRS tax transcripts, pay stubs, employment letters, or joint sponsors are required.

ina_320_required.title: Proof of Petitioner's U.S. Citizenship
ina_320_required.sub: Evidence establishing that the petitioning parent is a U.S. citizen

guide.intro: The child derives citizenship under INA Section 320 through the U.S. citizen parent. Proof of the parent's U.S. citizenship is mandatory.

sections.title: Accepted Evidence
sections.body: Provide a clear color copy of the petitioner's unexpired U.S. passport biographic page, U.S. birth certificate, Certificate of Naturalization, or Certificate of Citizenship.

ina_320_required.title: Proof of Legal & Physical Custody in the U.S.
ina_320_required.sub: Evidence that the child will reside with the citizen parent in the United States

guide.intro: INA Section 320 requires that the child will reside in the United States in the legal and physical custody of the U.S. citizen parent.

sections.title: Legal Custody
sections.body: Legal custody is established by the child's birth certificate (for married biological parents), a final court custody decree awarding legal custody to the citizen parent, or a legal adoption decree.

sections.title: Physical Residence in the U.S.
sections.body: Submit proof of the U.S. citizen parent's principal residence in the United States (lease, deed, utility bills) and a statement confirming that the child will reside with the parent upon arrival in the U.S.

sponsor_required.title: Form I-864, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Completed Affidavit of Support for stepchild or adult child beneficiary

guide.intro: Each sponsor must submit a separate, properly completed Form I-864. The petitioner must submit Form I-864 even when a joint sponsor is used.

sections.title: USCIS Form Integrity
sections.body: Download the latest version of Form I-864 directly from the USCIS website. Fill out all pages, leave no blank fields (use 'N/A' or 'None' where appropriate), and ensure it is signed. NVC will reject the form if pages are missing, the signature is photocopied/digital instead of wet-ink/original (if required by current post rules), or if the form edition is outdated.

sections.title: Household size and Income
sections.body: Ensure the household size on Part 5 matches the tax return information or is correctly adjusted. The sponsor's current individual annual income (Part 6) must align with the supporting employment letters, W-2s, and pay stubs. If the petitioner's income is $0, they must still file Form I-864 showing $0 income, and a joint sponsor will file a separate I-864.

sections.title: IR-2 Specific Rules (Stepchildren & Age 18+)
sections.body: Form I-864 is required for stepchildren and adult children (ages 18-20) who do not qualify for INA Section 320 automatic citizenship upon admission. Form I-864EZ may be used only if the petitioner meets income requirements using salary alone with no joint sponsors.

sponsor_required.title: Most Recent IRS Tax Transcript, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Preferred official tax evidence for the most recent tax year

guide.intro: An IRS tax transcript from the most recent tax year is the preferred tax evidence because it can be reviewed more efficiently than a copy of a tax return.

sections.title: Why IRS Transcripts are Preferred
sections.body: The NVC strongly prefers IRS Tax Transcripts over paper-filed Form 1040 returns because transcripts are verified directly by the IRS, reducing verification delays. It shows the Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), tax liability, and filing status clearly.

sections.title: How to Obtain
sections.body: The sponsor can obtain the transcript instantly by logging into their online IRS account via the 'Get Transcript Online' tool. If they cannot access the online tool, they must request it by mail using IRS Form 4506-T. Ensure you download the 'Tax Return Transcript' (not the Account Transcript).

sections.title: Alternative
sections.body: If an IRS transcript is genuinely unavailable, you must submit a complete, signed copy of the federal income tax return (Form 1040) along with all W-2s, 1099s, and supporting schedules.

sponsor_required.title: Proof of U.S. Status, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Evidence that the sponsor has qualifying U.S. immigration status

guide.intro: The IR-2 petitioner must be a U.S. citizen. A joint sponsor may be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or lawful permanent resident, as permitted by Form I-864 instructions.

sections.title: Accepted Citizenship Evidence
sections.body:
Provide a clear color scan of one of the following:
  • A current, unexpired U.S. passport biographic page.
  • U.S. birth certificate showing birth in the United States.
  • Certificate of Naturalization (Form N-550 or N-570).
  • Certificate of Citizenship (Form N-560 or N-561).

sections.title: Joint Sponsor (LPR Status)
sections.body: If the joint sponsor is a Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR), they must provide a clear color scan of both sides of their Permanent Resident Card (Green Card, Form I-551). The card must be unexpired.

sponsor_required.title: Proof of U.S. Domicile, ${sp}
sponsor_required.sub: Evidence of domicile in the United States or qualifying steps to re-establish it

guide.intro: Every Form I-864 sponsor must be domiciled in the United States or demonstrate qualifying steps to re-establish U.S. domicile no later than the intending immigrant's admission.

sections.title: What is Domicile?
sections.body: Domicile is the place where a sponsor has their principal, permanent home and intends to maintain it. For petitioners living in the U.S., a driver's license, utility bills, tax history, and employment records are sufficient.

sections.title: Petitioners Residing in Pakistan
sections.body:
If the U.S. citizen petitioner is currently living in Pakistan, they must provide strong documentary evidence that they have taken concrete steps to re-establish U.S. domicile before or at the same time the child enters the U.S. Acceptable evidence includes:
  • A U.S. residential lease agreement or proof of U.S. home ownership.
  • A signed employment contract or job offer in the U.S.
  • Documentation showing U.S. bank accounts, voter registration, and active driver's license.
  • Proof of enrolling children in U.S. schools.

sponsor_conditional.title: Complete Federal Tax Return, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Alternative when the most recent IRS tax transcript is unavailable or specifically requested

guide.intro: A complete copy of the most recent filed federal income tax return may be used instead of an IRS transcript or when NVC specifically requests the complete return.

sections.title: Complete Return Assembly
sections.body:
A complete return means you must include:
  • Form 1040 (all pages, signed and dated by the sponsor).
  • All W-2 and 1099 statements showing wages and earnings.
  • All schedules filed with the IRS (Schedule A, B, C, D, E, etc.).
If any schedule is missing, NVC will issue a rejection notice.

sponsor_conditional.title: W-2, 1099, and Relevant Tax Schedules, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Supporting records when needed to establish the sponsor's individual income

guide.intro: These records may be needed when a complete tax return is submitted, the sponsor filed jointly, or the transcript does not clearly establish the sponsor's individual qualifying income.

sections.title: Isolating Joint Filing Income
sections.body: If the sponsor filed a joint tax return with their spouse, their individual income must be verified separately. Uploading all individual W-2 and 1099 forms isolates the sponsor's own earnings from their spouse's earnings, ensuring they meet the 125% Federal Poverty Guidelines on their own.

sponsor_conditional.title: Current Pay Records, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Current income evidence when ongoing earnings must be established

guide.intro: Recent pay records can establish that the sponsor's qualifying income is current and continuing, especially when income changed after the most recent tax filing.

sections.title: Current Income Proof
sections.body: Provide consecutive pay stubs covering the last 6 months. Pay stubs must show the employer's name, employee name, gross wages, pay period, and year-to-date earnings. This is crucial if the sponsor's income has increased since their last tax filing or if they recently started a new job.

sponsor_conditional.title: Employment Verification Letter, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Supporting proof of current employment and compensation

guide.intro: An employment verification letter may support current qualifying income where employment evidence is needed.

sections.title: Letter Specifications
sections.body:
The letter must be printed on official company letterhead, dated within the last 60 days, and signed by an authorized supervisor or HR manager. It must state:
  • Dates of employment and job title.
  • Employment status (full-time, part-time, permanent).
  • Annual salary or hourly wage rate and average weekly hours.

sponsor_conditional.title: Asset Evidence, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Required only when qualifying assets are used to cover an income shortfall

guide.intro: Qualifying assets may be used when income alone is insufficient. Under 8 CFR 213a.2(c)(2)(iii)(B), for the child of a U.S. citizen, the net value of qualifying assets must equal at least THREE times (3x) the income shortfall (unlike other categories which require 5x).

sections.title: Three-Times (3x) Rule for Children
sections.body: Because the beneficiary is the child of a U.S. citizen, the total net value of assets must equal at least 3 times the difference between the sponsor's household income and the 125% HHS Poverty Guidelines threshold.

sections.title: Asset Valuation Requirements
sections.body: Provide proof of ownership, current valuation, and evidence that the asset can be converted to cash within 12 months without undue harm. For real estate, submit the deed, a professional appraisal, and a mortgage statement showing current equity. For bank accounts, submit 12 months of consecutive monthly statements.

sponsor_conditional.title: Tax Non-Filing Explanation, ${sp}
sponsor_conditional.sub: Required if the sponsor was not legally required to file the most recent federal tax return

guide.intro: A sponsor who did not file a federal tax return must explain why filing was not legally required.

sections.title: Filing Thresholds and Exemptions
sections.body: Sponsors who had no U.S. income or whose income fell below the IRS filing threshold must provide a written, signed statement citing the specific IRS code or threshold limits. If they were living abroad and did not file, they must explain this, keeping in mind that U.S. citizens are required to file taxes on worldwide income.

sponsor_recommended.title: Organized Sponsorship Packet, ${sp}
sponsor_recommended.sub: Affidavit form and supporting evidence grouped clearly by sponsor

guide.intro: Each sponsor's records should be kept separate and clearly labeled so the correct form and evidence are uploaded under the correct sponsor in CEAC.

sections.title: How to organize
sections.body: Group Form I-864, tax evidence, status evidence, domicile evidence, current-income evidence, and asset evidence for ${sp} into one clearly labeled folder structure.

household_conditional.title: Form I-864A, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Contract for a qualifying household member contributing income or assets

guide.intro: A qualifying household member whose income or assets are used completes and signs Form I-864A with the petitioning sponsor.

sections.title: Form I-864A Contract
sections.body: Form I-864A is a legally binding contract between the sponsor and the household member. The household member agrees to be jointly and severally liable for the financial support of the child beneficiary. Ensure all pages are submitted and signed.

household_conditional.title: Most Recent Tax Evidence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: IRS transcript or applicable federal return evidence for the household member

guide.intro: The household member must document the income or assets contributed through Form I-864A.

sections.title: Tax Records for Household Members
sections.body: Provide the IRS Tax Transcript for the household member's most recent tax year. If transcripts are not available, submit Form 1040 accompanied by W-2s and schedules.

household_conditional.title: Current Income Evidence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Proof that the household member's contributed income is current and continuing

guide.intro: Current income evidence should support the amount contributed by the household member on Form I-864A.

sections.title: Verifying Continuing Income
sections.body: Provide current pay stubs and employment letters for the household member. The income must be from a lawful source and expected to continue after the child immigrates.

household_conditional.title: Proof of Household Relationship or Shared Residence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Evidence establishing eligibility to contribute through Form I-864A

guide.intro: Depending on the household member category, evidence of a qualifying family relationship, shared residence, or both may be required.

sections.title: Establishing Household Linkage
sections.body: If the household member is the sponsor's spouse, sibling, child, or parent, submit birth certificates, marriage certificates, or adoption decrees. Also submit lease agreements, tax filings, or utility bills showing they share the same physical residence.

household_conditional.title: Household Member Asset Evidence, ${hm}
household_conditional.sub: Required only when the household member's assets are included

guide.intro: Include asset evidence only when the household member's qualifying assets are being used in the sponsorship calculation.

sections.title: What to establish
sections.body: Show ownership, net value after liabilities, and convertibility to cash within one year without undue hardship (3x multiplier applies for child beneficiary).

general_recommended.title: Prior-Year Tax Evidence Backup
general_recommended.sub: Additional prior-year records available if NVC requests them

guide.intro: The most recent tax year is the normal core evidence, but earlier records may be useful when income history is irregular or NVC requests additional documentation.

sections.title: When it may help
sections.body: Keep prior-year transcripts or returns available when recent income changed substantially, a filing extension or non-filing issue exists, or additional income history is requested.

general_recommended.title: Upload-Ready Financial Packet
general_recommended.sub: Clear, properly named files organized for CEAC upload

guide.intro: Preparing an upload-ready packet reduces classification, readability, and submission errors.

sections.title: File preparation
sections.body: Keep each file within CEAC's current size limit (<2 MB), use an accepted file type (PDF/JPG), make every page legible, and organize files separately for the petitioner, each joint sponsor, and each household member.

joint_sponsor_requirements.disclaimer: A joint sponsor or household member is ONLY applicable if Form I-864 is required (stepchildren and adult children ages 18-20). Children qualifying for automatic citizenship under INA Section 320 file Form I-864W and do not need a joint sponsor or household member.
guidance: Child Citizenship Act Exemption (INA Section 320): If the beneficiary is a biological or legally adopted child under age 18 who will reside in the legal and physical custody of the U.S. citizen parent, they file Form I-864W. No joint sponsor or household member is needed or permitted.

When Applicable: A joint sponsor or household member is only used for stepchildren or adult children (ages 18-20) when the U.S. citizen petitioner cannot meet the 125% HHS Poverty Guidelines (or 100% for active-duty military) on their own.

Joint Sponsor Requirements: A joint sponsor must be a U.S. citizen or LPR, at least 18 years old, and domiciled in the U.S. The joint sponsor must independently satisfy 125% of the HHS Poverty Guidelines for their household size plus the child. The petitioner's income cannot be combined with the joint sponsor's income.

Household Member (Form I-864A): An eligible relative living in the petitioner's principal residence (such as the petitioner's spouse or adult child) can combine income with the petitioner by signing Form I-864A.

Petitioner Always Required: Even when a joint sponsor is used, the petitioner must still submit their own signed Form I-864 and most recent tax transcript showing their individual income (even if $0).
joint_sponsor_requirements.source_basis: Form I-864 / I-864A instructions; INA Section 213A, INA Section 320 (Child Citizenship Act of 2000), 8 CFR 213a.2.

howItWorks: NVC places the IR-2 case in the interview scheduling queue immediately upon issuing the Documentary Qualification (DQ) notice.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad releases available immigrant visa interview appointment blocks to NVC on a monthly basis.
NVC assigns appointments to documentarily qualified cases strictly in first-in, first-out order based on the DQ date.
As an Immediate Relative (IR-2) category, there is no numerical quota or Visa Bulletin priority date wait.
When an interview date is assigned, NVC emails the official Interview Appointment Letter (P4) containing the date, time, and instructions.
Do NOT schedule the panel physician medical examination until you have received the official appointment letter.

guideSteps.label: Step 1 of 5
guideSteps.heading: What is the polio vaccination requirement?
guideSteps.instruction: Typical cases from Pakistan will require a polio certificate for the medical examination. Therefore, it is highly recommended and advisable to obtain it beforehand to avoid any delays in your child's medical process.

visual.title: Why this is required
visual.sub: The U.S. requires polio vaccination documentation from applicants from polio-endemic countries. This is administered at an approved vaccination site, not a general clinic.

guideSteps.label: Step 2 of 5
guideSteps.heading: Where to get vaccinated
guideSteps.instruction: Polio vaccinations for visa purposes must be obtained from an approved government vaccination post or official WHO-designated site. Do not use a private clinic unless it is specifically on the approved list.
guideSteps.note: Do not go to a general doctor or hospital for this, you must use a government-approved site for the certificate to be accepted.

visual.title: Approved Vaccination Sites
visual.sub: Government immunization centres in major cities typically administer this vaccine and issue the official certificate. Contact your local district health office or check with your child's panel physician for the nearest site.

guideSteps.label: Step 3 of 5
guideSteps.heading: What the certificate looks like
guideSteps.instruction: The official polio vaccination certificate is typically a printed card or letter issued at the vaccination site. It should include your child's name, vaccination date, and the type of vaccine received.

visual.title: Certificate Details to Verify
items: Your child's full legal name (matching passport)
Date of vaccination
Vaccine type, oral polio vaccine (OPV)
Official stamp or signature

guideSteps.label: Step 4 of 5
guideSteps.heading: Timing, when to get vaccinated
guideSteps.instruction: Get your child's polio vaccination at least a few days before your child's medical exam appointment so you can bring the original certificate to the exam. The panel physician will record it as part of your child's medical packet.
guideSteps.note: Do not get vaccinated the same day as the medical exam unless your child's panel physician specifically confirms this is acceptable.

visual.title: Recommended Timing
visual.sub: Vaccinate -> Receive certificate -> Bring original to medical exam. Budget at least 1-3 days between vaccination and your child's scheduled medical exam date.

guideSteps.label: Step 5 of 5
guideSteps.heading: Bring the original certificate to your child's medical exam
guideSteps.instruction: Bring the original polio vaccination certificate to your child's medical exam appointment. Your child's panel physician will review it and include documentation in the sealed medical packet sent to the embassy.

Prepare the child's documents, verify translations and consistency with the records submitted through CEAC, and organize any additional documents required for a biological-child, stepchild, or other qualifying relationship case.
steps.who: Child Beneficiary (with parent or guardian assistance)
steps.timeline: 2-3 days (estimated; obtaining missing or updated records may take longer)
actions: Collect the child's original or certified civil documents
Collect the petitioner's and financial sponsors' supporting documents
Prepare relationship-specific documents for the child's case, if applicable
Obtain required police, court, or other records based on the child's age and history
Prepare English translations and photocopies
Compare the originals with the documents submitted through CEAC
Organize the documents into clearly labelled sections

items.title: Child's Current Passport and Relevant Prior Passports
items.sub: Current unexpired passport, biographic-page photocopy, and relevant prior passports

sections.c: Bring the child's current, original, unexpired passport. It should be valid for at least six months beyond the intended date of entry into the United States. Also bring relevant prior passports, especially those containing previous U.S. visas, entry or exit stamps, visa refusals, or other relevant immigration and travel history.

Bring one clear photocopy of the current passport's biographic page (the page showing the photograph, name, date of birth, passport number, and expiry date). Keep it separate from the original passport.

Check that the child's name, date of birth, place of birth, and passport details are consistent with the DS-260 and civil documents. For a minor, the parent or legal guardian should follow the applicable passport-signing and issuance rules; do not assume that the child must personally sign the passport.

items.title: Child's Original Birth Certificate or Accepted Alternate Record
items.sub: Primary civil record establishing the child's identity and recorded parentage

sections.c:
Bring the child's original Birth Registration Certificate or a certified copy issued by the relevant Pakistani local government authority. Depending on the place of registration, this may be issued by the Union Council, Municipal Corporation, Capital Development Authority (CDA) in Islamabad, or Cantonment Board.

The U.S. Department of State's Pakistan reciprocity schedule also identifies the NADRA Child Registration Certificate (CRC, commonly called the B-Form) and Family Registration Certificate (FRC) as alternate documents. Bring the relevant original or officially issued record that was submitted to NVC, together with any additional record requested in your case.

Bring the original or certified civil record, an English translation where the document is not in English, and a clear photocopy. Keep the original, translation, and photocopy together. Make sure all pages and any information printed on the reverse are included.

sections.t: If the birth was not registered
sections.c: If the child's birth was not registered, bring the Non-Availability Certificate (NAC) and the secondary evidence submitted to NVC or requested by the Embassy. Depending on the case, this may include a CRC/B-Form, FRC, school records, hospital or vaccination records, or other contemporaneous records. Do not assume that an affidavit or a single secondary record automatically replaces the required civil evidence.

Check the child's full name, date and place of birth, and the names of both parents against the passport, DS-260, petition, and CEAC documents. If spellings, dates, or parent details differ, prepare the official supporting records that explain the discrepancy.

items.title: Birth Certificates for the Child Beneficiary's Children, If Applicable
items.sub: Required if the principal applicant has children, including children who are not immigrating

sections.c: If the child beneficiary has children, bring the original or certified birth certificates for all of them, including those who are not immigrating with the applicant. Include English translations and photocopies where required.
This requirement applies only if the principal applicant has children. It does not mean that every IR-2 applicant must bring the birth certificates of their siblings.

items.title: Petitioner's Birth Certificate or Relevant Relationship Evidence
items.sub: Additional family-based document listed in the Islamabad pre-interview checklist

sections.c: For family-based immigrant visa cases, the Islamabad pre-interview checklist asks for the petitioner's original birth certificate, an English translation, and a photocopy. Bring the petitioner's birth certificate or the corresponding official civil record available for the petitioner's place of birth.

sections.t: How it relates to an IR-2 case
sections.c: In an IR-2 case, the petitioner's birth certificate is not normally the primary document establishing the petitioner's relationship to the child. The child's own birth record and the relationship evidence applicable to the approved I-130 are central. Keep the petitioner's birth certificate as part of the Islamabad family-based checklist, and bring any additional relationship evidence requested for the case.
If the petitioner's birth certificate is not in English, bring the original or certified record, a complete English translation, and a photocopy.

items.title: Police Certificates, If Required
items.sub: Police certificate(s), if required based on the applicant's age, nationality, residence history, and criminal history

sections.c: Do not assume that every IR-2 child needs a police certificate. The U.S. Embassy Islamabad specifically requires an original Pakistan police certificate from applicants older than 16 years of age. Police certificates may also be required from other countries based on the applicant's residence history and applicable Department of State rules.

The Pakistani document is called a Character Certificate. It is issued by a Police Facilitation Center or local police office in the applicant's home province or current province of residence, as listed on the CNIC. The issuing procedure and format vary by location.

If the child has lived in other countries, check the applicable residence-duration and age requirements for each country. Follow the current Islamabad post instructions for obtaining an updated certificate. The post-specific checklist has additional one-year update conditions in certain circumstances, while general Department of State guidance describes a two-year validity period with an exception for some former countries of residence. Do not apply a single validity rule to every country and situation.

When a police certificate is required, bring the original certificate and any required English translation and photocopy. Follow the Embassy's instructions for updated certificates; general Department of State guidance says not to send new or updated police certificates to NVC.

items.title: NVC Interview Appointment Letter
items.sub: Printed copy of the child's immigrant visa interview appointment notice

sections.c: Print and bring the child's NVC interview appointment letter. Check that the applicant's name, case details, interview date, and location are correct.

If a parent, guardian, or other authorized person will accompany the minor child, check the Embassy's current accompanying-person rules and appointment-letter requirements. The Islamabad instructions state that anyone whose name is not listed on the appointment letter will not be allowed to enter.

items.title: Form I-864, Petitioner's Affidavit of Support
items.sub: The petitioner's completed Affidavit of Support package

sections.c: For this family-based immigrant visa case, prepare the petitioner's completed and signed Form I-864 and the supporting evidence requested in the Islamabad pre-interview checklist. The petitioner must submit the appropriate Affidavit of Support even if a joint sponsor is also being used.

If the petitioner's income does not meet the applicable requirements and a joint sponsor is used, the petitioner must still submit the petitioner's own I-864. The joint sponsor must submit a separate I-864 and supporting evidence.

Check that the form is complete, signed, and consistent with the version submitted through CEAC. Follow the current Form I-864 instructions for the permitted signature format. Do not assume that every case requires a wet-ink original unless the Embassy or case-specific instructions say so.

items.title: Petitioner's Most Recent Tax and Income Evidence
items.sub: IRS tax transcript or federal tax return and related income records

sections.c: The Islamabad family-based checklist asks for a photocopy of the sponsor's IRS tax transcript or most recent U.S. federal income tax return, together with related W-2s. Bring the relevant evidence for the petitioner's financial sponsorship and keep it organized with Form I-864.

If a more recent tax year has ended since the financial documents were submitted to NVC, consider preparing the latest available tax evidence. Follow any specific request from NVC or the Embassy about updated financial documents.

If the petitioner's employment or income has changed significantly since the I-864 was submitted, additional current evidence may help explain the sponsor's financial circumstances. Examples include recent pay statements and an employer verification letter. These are supporting examples, not a universal substitute for the required tax evidence.

items.title: Petitioner's U.S. Immigration Status and Domicile Evidence
items.sub: Evidence of the petitioner's qualifying U.S. status and U.S. domicile

sections.c: Bring a photocopy of the petitioner's evidence of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent resident status, as applicable. Examples include a U.S. passport biographic page, U.S. birth certificate, Certificate of Naturalization, Certificate of Citizenship, or both sides of a Permanent Resident Card.

Prepare evidence that the petitioner is domiciled in the United States. Depending on the circumstances, this may include a U.S. residence lease or mortgage statement, utility bills, employment records, U.S. driver's license, bank statements, voter registration, or property records.

If the petitioner currently lives outside the United States, prepare evidence showing that the petitioner has maintained U.S. domicile or has taken concrete steps to re-establish it no later than the child's immigration. Examples may include a U.S. job offer, a signed residential lease, or other credible relocation arrangements. A joint sponsor does not remove the petitioner's own domicile requirement.

items.title: Joint Sponsor or Household Member Package
items.sub: Required only if a joint sponsor or household member is included in the financial sponsorship

sections.c: If a joint sponsor is used, prepare the joint sponsor's separately completed and signed Form I-864 and the supporting documents requested for that sponsor. These generally include the most recent IRS tax transcript or federal tax return, related W-2s, evidence of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent resident status, and evidence of U.S. domicile.

If a household member's income is being used, prepare the completed and signed Form I-864A where required, along with the household member's relevant tax and current income evidence. Check that the household member qualifies under the I-864A rules and that the documents match the package submitted to NVC.
Bring the documents applicable to the actual sponsorship arrangement in the child's case. Do not prepare a joint-sponsor or household-member package if no such person is being used.

groups.label: Bring, Interview Day and Conditional Documents

items.title: DS-260 Confirmation Page
items.sub: Printed Immigrant Visa Application confirmation page

sections.c: Bring the printed DS-260 confirmation page with its barcode for the child. This confirms that the child's online immigrant visa application was submitted.
Review the child's DS-260 details and check that the information is consistent with the passport, birth certificate, relationship evidence, and other civil documents submitted through CEAC.
Download and print the confirmation page from the Consular Electronic Application Center (CEAC) after the child's DS-260 has been submitted.

items.title: Two Recent Visa Photographs of the Child
items.sub: Two identical 5 cm × 5 cm color photographs

sections.c: Bring two recent, identical color photographs of the child, taken within the period specified by the U.S. visa photo requirements. Islamabad requires two photographs of every person applying for a visa. The photographs must measure 5 cm × 5 cm (2 inches × 2 inches) and meet the current U.S. visa photograph specifications.

The photograph should have a plain white or off-white background, show the child facing the camera, and meet the official head-size and image-quality requirements. Do not use eyeglasses. Follow the official photo guidance for infants and young children who may not be able to maintain a neutral expression or position.

Use a photo studio familiar with U.S. visa photograph specifications. Confirm the dimensions and requirements before printing. The six photographs requested for the Islamabad medical examination are a separate requirement and should not be confused with the two photographs for the visa interview.

items.title: Medical Examination Results
items.sub: Sealed medical results provided by the panel physician or sent directly to the Embassy

sections.c: The child must complete the immigrant visa medical examination with a physician approved by U.S. Embassy Islamabad. The physician will either send the results directly to the Embassy or provide the applicant with a sealed envelope. Confirm the result-delivery method with the clinic.

sections.t: If a sealed envelope is provided
sections.c: Do not open the sealed medical envelope. If the panel physician gives the results to the applicant in a sealed envelope, keep it sealed and bring it to the interview for the consular officer.

The panel physician will give the applicant any X-rays taken. Islamabad's instructions state that X-rays generally do not need to be brought to the interview unless the applicant has tuberculosis. The applicant must carry the X-rays when travelling to the United States for the first time. Keep relevant medical records and test results available if requested.

items.title: Stepchild Relationship Records
items.sub: Required when the petitioner qualifies as the child's stepparent

sections.c: Bring the original marriage certificate of the petitioner and the child's biological parent. Islamabad specifically requests this document for applicants immigrating as a petitioner's stepchild. Bring the required English translation and a photocopy.

The marriage creating the stepparent-stepchild relationship must have taken place before the child turned 18 for the relationship to qualify under the applicable immigration definition of a child. Check that the marriage date and the child's date of birth support the relationship claimed in the approved I-130 petition.

Bring divorce, annulment, or death records showing the legal termination of all previous marriages of either the petitioner or the child's biological parent, as applicable. Include English translations and photocopies. Records showing that the child's own earlier marriages ended, and evidence that a stepparent relationship continued after a marriage ended, are listed separately below.

items.title: Additional Biological Parent-Child Relationship Evidence
items.sub: Required only when the child's relationship or eligibility requires additional proof

sections.c: For a biological-child case, the child's birth certificate will generally be central evidence of the parent-child relationship. However, additional records may be needed if the petition involves a biological father and the child was born outside marriage, if the parentage details are incomplete, or if the approved petition relied on additional evidence to establish the qualifying relationship.

Bring the original or certified versions of the relationship evidence that was submitted with the I-130 or requested by USCIS, NVC, or the Embassy. Depending on the circumstances, this may include parents' marriage records, legitimation records, court orders, or contemporaneous records showing the claimed parent-child relationship.
Do not treat every example as mandatory for every biological-child case. Use the documents relevant to the child's actual relationship, the approved petition, and any case-specific request.

items.title: Adoption or Guardianship Records, If Applicable
items.sub: Requires careful review under U.S. immigration law; Pakistani guardianship alone does not establish an adoptive parent-child relationship

sections.c: If the approved immigration petition relies on an adoption or another qualifying legal relationship, bring the relevant original or certified adoption decree, custody records, and supporting evidence requested for the case. Include English translations and photocopies.

For an adopted child, the general rule is a full and final adoption before the child turned 16, together with two years of legal custody and two years of joint residence with the adoptive parent. A narrow exception may apply to siblings adopted before 18. Confirm which rule the approved petition relied on and bring the records that prove the relevant dates.

The U.S. Department of State's Pakistan reciprocity schedule states that adoption certificates are unavailable in Pakistan and that Pakistani guardianship orders do not create a permanent parent-child relationship for U.S. immigration purposes. A Pakistani guardianship order or affidavit must not be presented as automatically establishing an IR-2 adoptive relationship.

If the child is being petitioned based on adoption, guardianship, or an adoption intended to be finalized in the United States, obtain case-specific guidance from a qualified U.S. immigration attorney or U.S. Embassy Islamabad. Bring the documents relevant to the approved petition and follow any specific Embassy instructions.

items.title: Parents' Marriage or Marital History Records
items.sub: Required only when relevant to the claimed relationship or specifically requested

sections.c: If the child's case relies on a stepparent relationship, bring the petitioner's marriage certificate to the child's biological parent and the termination records for any previous marriages of either parent. For other biological-child cases, bring marriage or marital-history records when they were used to establish the relationship or are requested by the Embassy.

For a Pakistani Muslim marriage, the relevant records may include the original Urdu Nikah Nama and the Marriage Registration Certificate (MRC) issued by the appropriate local authority. Bring the required English translation and photocopies. Document formats and issuing authorities can vary.

Where a prior marriage ended, bring the applicable original or certified divorce, annulment, or death record, together with its English translation and photocopy. For Pakistani Muslim divorces, the Department of State reciprocity schedule explains the applicable 90-day Union Council process and the Divorce Registration Certificate.

items.title: Name Change or Identity-Linking Records
items.sub: Required when names, spellings, dates, or identity details differ across records

sections.c: Bring original or certified official records that explain differences in the child's or petitioner's name, spelling, date of birth, or other identity details across the passport, birth certificate, NADRA records, DS-260, and petition. Depending on the issue, this may include a court order, official correction record, or other recognized identity-linking document.

An affidavit alone should not be assumed to correct an official civil record or resolve every identity discrepancy. Bring the official supporting documents relevant to the difference and follow any case-specific instructions.

items.title: Court and Criminal Records
items.sub: Required if the child has an applicable arrest, charge, conviction, or court history

sections.c: If the child has ever been arrested, charged, or convicted, bring the applicable original or certified court and criminal records, including records of the final disposition. Include English translations and photocopies where required.

Do not assume that a police certificate replaces court records when court or criminal records are required. If a record is unavailable, follow the relevant country reciprocity instructions and obtain case-specific guidance.

items.title: Military Service Records
items.sub: Required only if the applicant has served in a country's military

sections.c: If the applicant has served in any country's military, prepare the available military service, discharge, or retirement records, together with English translations and photocopies where required.

The Pakistan reciprocity schedule lists military records as unavailable but notes that a discharge certificate is issued upon discharge, retirement, or resignation from military service. If this applies, bring the available discharge certificate and follow the Embassy's instructions for any additional record.

items.title: Passport Delivery Registration Confirmation
items.sub: Proof of the required online passport return or pickup registration

sections.c: Keep a printed or accessible copy of the passport delivery registration confirmation and the selected document pickup or return details. The registration must be completed through the current portal linked by the Embassy.

Check that the child's case and passport information, contact details, and delivery or pickup selection are accurate. Follow the current portal and appointment instructions if the registration confirmation is not issued as a printable document.
Use the official U.S. visa scheduling and passport return registration portal linked from the U.S. Embassy Islamabad immigrant visa instructions.

items.title: Proof That the Child Is Unmarried
items.sub: Declared on the DS-260, with a local single-status record if the post asks for one

sections.c: An IR-2 or CR-2 beneficiary must be unmarried when the petition is filed and must remain unmarried until the visa is issued. The child's marital status is declared on the DS-260.

Bring the printed DS-260 confirmation page showing the unmarried status. Where the Embassy asks for civil proof as well, obtain the single-status or non-marriage record from the authority it names for the child's district, and bring the English translation and a photocopy.
If the child marries before the visa is issued, the IR-2 or CR-2 basis for the petition ends. Notify USCIS or the National Visa Center as soon as that happens instead of waiting for the interview.

items.title: Termination of the Child's Own Prior Marriages, If Any
items.sub: Required only if the child beneficiary was previously married

sections.c: If the child was married before, bring the original or certified divorce decree, annulment decree, or death certificate showing that the marriage ended legally, together with the English translation and a photocopy. These are the child's own records, not the parents'.
Confirm the termination date agrees with the DS-260 and with the statement that the child is unmarried now. Differences between the two are usually raised at the interview.

items.title: Custody Order and Non-Accompanying Parent Consent
items.sub: Required when the child immigrates with only one parent or guardian

sections.c: Bring the original legal custody documents and court orders, and the written consent of the child's other parent authorizing the immigration, with that parent's identity document. Include English translations and photocopies where required.

Where the other parent has died, cannot be located, or has had custody terminated, bring the record that establishes that fact, such as a death certificate, court order, or other civil record. Do not leave the requirement unaddressed.

Consent formats, notarization, and accompanying-parent expectations vary by case. Check the Embassy's current checklist and obtain case-specific guidance from a qualified U.S. immigration attorney where the other parent's position is disputed.

items.title: Evidence of a Continuing Stepparent-Stepchild Relationship
items.sub: Required where the marriage that created the step-relationship has since ended

sections.c: A step-relationship can still qualify after the marriage ended through divorce or death, but only if a genuine stepparent-stepchild relationship continued afterwards. Check that the marriage took place before the child turned 18 and note the date the marriage ended, because the records you bring should cover the period after it.

Bring records created during the period after the marriage ended that show an ongoing relationship, such as letters or messages, call or video-call records, visit and travel records, school or medical records showing the stepparent's involvement, and proof of financial support.
Form I-864 alone does not establish a continuing stepparent-stepchild relationship. Financial sponsorship and the existence of the family relationship are two separate questions.

items.title: Labeled Folder System
items.sub: Separate originals, translations, photocopies, and conditional relationship records

sections.c: A clearly organized document packet helps the parent or guardian assist the child and makes it easier to present the requested records at the consular window.

• Use lightweight folders or clearly labelled document sleeves.
  • Separate Passport and Appointment / Child's Civil Records / Relationship Evidence / Financial Sponsor / Conditional Records / Medical and Courier.
  • Keep each original or certified document together with its English translation and photocopy.
  • Keep conditional documents separate so they can be produced when relevant.

items.title: Complete Photocopy Set
items.sub: One clear photocopy of each required civil and supporting document

sections.c: The Islamabad checklist requests photocopies alongside several original or certified civil records. The Embassy may retain photocopies while returning original documents after the interview.

Make sure copies are complete, readable, and include both sides of documents where information, stamps, or endorsements appear on the reverse. Keep translations paired with the corresponding original.

items.title: CEAC-to-Original Match Check
items.sub: Verify that the interview documents match the records submitted to NVC

sections.c: Compare each original or certified civil document with the corresponding document submitted through CEAC. Islamabad states that, in most cases, required and updated documents must also be uploaded through CEAC before the interview. Follow any case-specific instructions about updated records.

Confirm names, dates of birth, parent details, issuing authorities, translations, document completeness, and any police-certificate requirements. Pay particular attention to the child's birth record and the relationship evidence supporting the approved I-130.

Confirm whether the case involves a biological parent, stepparent, or another qualifying relationship. Include only the applicable supporting records, such as a step-parent marriage certificate, prior-marriage termination records, or adoption-related documents where legally relevant.

steps.step_description: The child's immigrant visa interview takes place at U.S. Embassy Islamabad. Review what to bring, understand the interview-day process, and prepare for age-appropriate questions. A minor child may be accompanied by one person, subject to the Embassy's entry requirements.
steps.step_short_description: What to expect on interview day
actions: Plan to arrive at the Embassy approximately 20-30 minutes before your scheduled appointment
Pass security (NO electronics)
Submit documents at window
Fingerprints taken, if required for the applicant's age
Wait for consular officer call
Take oath, or have it completed on your child's behalf if they are under 14
Participate in the interview with age-appropriate assistance where permitted
Answer questions honestly
Receive the officer's instructions or case outcome

launch_module.heading: Step-by-step guide from arrival to outcome
cues: Arrival timing and embassy entry is strict
Consular interview flow and common questions
Possible outcomes and what happens next

tutorial.label: Step 1 of 8
tutorial.heading: Prepare the night before
tutorial.instruction: The night before the interview, organize the child's complete document packet. Confirm that the interview appointment letter is printed, the child's passport and required original civil documents are ready, and transport to the Embassy is arranged. If a parent or guardian will accompany the child, confirm that the person's name is included on the appointment letter.
tutorial.visual:
Night-before checklist
Appointment letter printed Ready
Document packet organized Ready
Transport arranged Confirmed
Passport photos packed Ready
Originals and copies separated Done

tutorial.label: Step 2 of 8
tutorial.heading: Arrive early, embassy entry is strict
tutorial.instruction: Arrive at the embassy at least 20-30 minutes before your scheduled appointment time. Embassy security queues can be slow. Latecomers may not be admitted for their scheduled slot.
tutorial.note: Do not carry electronics beyond what is permitted by the embassy. Check the specific embassy's guidelines on phones and devices before arrival.
tutorial.visual:
Arrival guidance
Plan for 20-30 minutes of buffer time. Factor in travel to the Diplomatic Enclave, transport arrangements, and security screening at U.S. Embassy Islamabad.
Earlier is always safer than exactly on time

tutorial.label: Step 3 of 8
tutorial.heading: Security screening and document intake
tutorial.instruction: At entry, your child's appointment letter and passport will be checked. You will pass through security screening. Some items, including certain electronics, may need to be left outside or checked in.
tutorial.visual:
Entry sequence
Appointment letter check at gate
Security screening (bag + personal)
Document receipt / number assignment
Wait in designated area

tutorial.label: Step 4 of 8
tutorial.heading: Biometrics, fingerprints and photo
tutorial.instruction:
Fingerprinting is generally required for immigrant visa applicants aged 14 and older. In limited cases, children aged 7 or older may also be asked to provide fingerprints. For applicants under 14, a parent or legal guardian may complete the required oath and biometric signature on the child's behalf.

Your child must still follow the applicable interview attendance instructions, even if they are not required to provide fingerprints.
tutorial.visual:
Biometric collection
Fingerprints are scanned digitally when they are required, and a digital photograph is taken. This takes only a few minutes. Follow the staff instructions exactly.

tutorial.label: Step 5 of 8
tutorial.heading: The consular interview window
tutorial.instruction: The child may be asked questions about their identity, relationship with the petitioner, family background, and plans in the United States. Questions will depend on the child's age, circumstances, and case history. A minor may receive assistance from an authorized accompanying person where permitted, but the child should answer in their own words when able.
tutorial.note: The child's answers should be truthful and consistent with the DS-260 and submitted civil documents. Do not memorize scripted answers or guess when unsure.
tutorial.visual:
Common IR-2 child interview topics
What is your name and when were you born?
Who is petitioning for you?
How do you know the petitioner?
When did you last speak to or see the petitioner?
Who do you currently live with?
Where will you live in the United States?
Have you travelled to the United States before?

tutorial.label: Step 6 of 8
tutorial.heading: Document review at the window
tutorial.instruction: The consular officer may ask to see the child's original civil documents and other supporting evidence. Present them calmly and in the order requested. Having a well-organized packet makes this faster and smoother.
tutorial.visual:
Documents to have ready
Child's current passport and relevant prior passports
Child's original birth certificate
Petitioner's birth certificate or other relevant relationship evidence
Original or certified adoption or custody documents, if applicable
Petitioner's marriage certificate and relevant prior marriage records, if the petitioner is a stepparent
Police certificate, if required
Form I-864 and current financial sponsorship evidence
DS-260 confirmation page and two visa photographs
Required English translations and photocopies

tutorial.label: Step 7 of 8
tutorial.heading: Stay calm, the officer is doing their job
tutorial.instruction: Consular officers ask direct questions. Their tone is professional, not personal. Nervousness is expected and normal. Answer clearly and calmly. If you do not understand a question, politely ask for clarification.
tutorial.visual: Answer only what is asked. Be honest. Be calm. Be concise. You have prepared for this, trust your preparation.

tutorial.label: Step 8 of 8
tutorial.heading: Possible outcomes after the interview
tutorial.instruction: The officer will indicate the outcome at the window or shortly after. After the interview, your child's application may be approved, refused under applicable law (including 221(g) where applicable), or require further administrative processing before a final determination is completed. If you were given a 221(g) refusal letter, continue to Step 10 for Rahvana's AP guidance.

Possible case outcomes
Approved, visa issuance processing begins Approved
221(g) refusal, documents or administrative processing required Further action
Refused under another legal ground, review the written notice Legal ground

doc_relationship.title: Relationship Evidence
doc_relationship.sub: Proof the marriage is genuine and entered in good faith

sections.title: Why this matters
sections.htmlContent: USCIS adjudicators will assess whether the marriage is bona fide, entered in good faith for a genuine life together, not primarily to obtain immigration benefits. Evidence across multiple categories significantly strengthens the case.

sections.title: Strong evidence categories
sections.htmlContent:
Gather evidence across as many of these categories as possible:

  • Communication history, WhatsApp/call logs, screenshots of messages over time, email correspondence showing an ongoing relationship
  • Photos together, wedding photos, casual photos, photos across different dates and locations, family gatherings
  • Travel history, plane tickets, boarding passes, hotel bookings showing in-person visits
  • Shared finances, joint bank account statements, shared bills, financial transfers between spouses
  • Shared residence, lease agreements, utility bills, or mail showing a shared address
  • Family evidence, children together, family photos that show integration into each other's families
  • Affidavits, signed statements from family members or friends who personally know the couple and can attest to the relationship

sections.title: For the I-130 stage specifically
sections.htmlContent:
At the USCIS I-130 filing stage, the petitioner submits the I-130 along with supporting evidence. A strong bona fide marriage package typically includes:

  • At least 3-5 photos showing the couple together across different occasions
  • Evidence of ongoing communication (call logs or chat screenshots with metadata)
  • Evidence of at least one in-person visit (travel documentation)
  • Affidavits if direct joint evidence is limited

There is no single "required" evidence list from USCIS, the goal is to present a convincing overall picture of a genuine relationship. More varied evidence across categories is better than one large category alone.

sections.title: What to avoid
sections.htmlContent:
• Do not submit hundreds of pages of chat history, curate and organize
  • Avoid submitting only one type of evidence (e.g. photos only)
  • Ensure affidavits are signed, dated, and specific about how the writer knows the couple
  • Do not use generic template affidavits, they are easily spotted and carry little weight

doc_prior_marriage.title: Prior Marriage Termination Proof
doc_prior_marriage.sub: Required if either spouse had a previous marriage

sections.title: When this applies
sections.htmlContent:
This document is required if either the petitioner or the beneficiary was previously married. USCIS must confirm that every prior marriage ended legally before the current marriage began.

If neither spouse has a prior marriage, this item does not apply to your case.

sections.title: Accepted termination documents
sections.htmlContent:
• Divorce decree or divorce certificate, final court order ending the prior marriage
  • Annulment order, court order declaring the marriage void
  • Death certificate, if the prior spouse is deceased

sections.title: Pakistan-specific, divorce
sections.htmlContent:
In Pakistan, divorce proceedings vary by religious law. For Muslims, the process typically involves:

  • Talaq, the husband's pronouncement, registered with the Union Council, followed by a mandatory 90-day reconciliation period (iddat); Union Council issues a divorce certificate after this period
  • Khula, wife-initiated dissolution through Family Court; court issues the final decree
  • Judicial divorce, through Family Court; court issues the final decree

Important: For talaq, the divorce is not legally effective in Pakistan until the 90-day reconciliation period expires and the Union Council issues the divorce certificate. Ensure you have the final certificate, not just the initial notice.

sections.title: Translation requirement
sections.htmlContent: All divorce decrees and termination documents in Urdu or other non-English languages must be accompanied by a full certified English translation.

doc_translations.title: Translations
doc_translations.sub: Certified English translations of non-English documents

sections.title: USCIS translation requirement
sections.htmlContent: USCIS requires that every document not in English be accompanied by a full certified English translation. This applies to all stages, I-130, NVC, and consular.

sections.title: What "certified translation" means
sections.htmlContent:
USCIS defines a certified translation as one accompanied by a signed statement from the translator certifying:

  • They are competent to translate from the source language to English
  • The translation is accurate and complete to the best of their ability

The translator does not need to be a licensed professional or a notary, but they must not be the applicant or petitioner themselves.

sections.title: Documents that need translation
sections.htmlContent:
• Nikah Nama, typically in Urdu; full translation required
  • NADRA MRC, bilingual, but full translation of the Urdu portions is recommended to avoid questions
  • Birth certificate, if issued in Urdu or regional language
  • Divorce decree, if in Urdu or Sindhi etc.
  • Any other civil documents submitted to USCIS or the NVC

sections.title: Practical tips
sections.htmlContent:
• Use a translation service that issues a formal certification letter on their letterhead, it is more persuasive than a plain self-attestation
  • Keep the translated document together with the original, submit them as a pair
  • Do not translate only part of a document, the entire document must be translated

doc_passport_photos.title: Passport Photos
doc_passport_photos.sub: Required at consular and visa application stages

sections.title: When these are needed
sections.htmlContent:
Passport photos are not required for the USCIS I-130 petition filing. They are required at later stages:

  • The DS-260 immigrant visa application (online form submitted to the NVC)
  • At the consular interview, the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad typically requires passport-size photos

Gather them closer to those stages rather than now.

sections.title: U.S. visa photo specifications
sections.htmlContent:
• 2 × 2 inches (51 × 51 mm)
  • White or off-white plain background
  • Taken within the last 6 months
  • Full front view, neutral expression, eyes open
  • No glasses (as of 2016 U.S. visa photo rules)
  • Head coverings only for religious reasons, and must not obscure the face

The DS-260 online application accepts a digital photo upload, check the U.S. State Department's photo upload tool and specifications at the time of filing.

doc_name_change.title: Name Change or Identity Discrepancy Evidence
doc_name_change.sub: Resolving spelling and profile mismatches across records

sections.title: Handling Name Mismatches
sections.htmlContent: Mismatches across your birth certificate, national ID, school records, or passport can trigger delays or Requests for Evidence in any country, so it's worth sorting these out before you file.

sections.title: Civil Registry Correction
sections.htmlContent: To correct a name or date of birth, visit your country's civil registry office with supporting documents like matriculation certificates, older passports, or court decrees. In Pakistan, this means a NADRA office, which will issue a revised CNIC/NICOP and FRC. Note that NADRA generally only corrects English-spelling mistakes through this process, a full name change requires the separate procedure below.

sections.title: Gazette Notification & Deed Poll
sections.htmlContent: For a full legal name change in Pakistan, you'll need a notarized affidavit, a published notice in local newspapers, and registration with the official Gazette of Pakistan. The published Gazette notice is what carries real legal weight, it's what banks, passport offices, and other institutions will actually ask to see.

sections.title: Sworn Affidavits
sections.htmlContent: If your records genuinely can't be corrected, a notarized affidavit from close relatives explaining the mismatch can serve as backup evidence in most jurisdictions.

marriage-cert-hh.title: Marriage Certificate, Household Member
marriage-cert-hh.intro: Establishes the spousal relationship between the household member and the petitioner.

sections.title: What this is
sections.body: The civil marriage certificate proving that the household member is legally married to the petitioner. For Pakistan cases, this is the Nikah Nama and/or NADRA MRC.

sections.title: Why it is needed
sections.body: When the petitioner's spouse is acting as a household member contributing income through Form I-864A, the marriage must be documented to support that household connection.

sections.title: Translation
sections.body: The Nikah Nama (in Urdu) requires a full certified English translation.

shared-residence.title: Proof of Shared Residence
shared-residence.intro: Demonstrates that the household member and the petitioner share the same household address.

sections.title: What this is
sections.body: Documents showing a shared residential address between the petitioner and the household member. This reinforces the household income contribution basis.

sections.title: Accepted examples
sections.body:
• Lease agreement naming both parties
  • Utility bills addressed to the same household
  • Bank statements or tax returns showing the same address
  • Official correspondence addressed to both at the same address

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: The household member concept in I-864A depends on a genuine shared household. Residence proof strengthens the basis for including their income.

id-doc-hh.title: Identity Document, Household Member
id-doc-hh.intro: Confirms the identity of the household member named in the I-864A.

sections.title: What to provide
sections.body: A government-issued identity document for the household member. For Pakistan cases, this is typically the CNIC (Computerized National Identity Card) or a passport biographic page.

sections.title: Consistency
sections.body: The name on the identity document must match exactly the name used in CEAC and on the I-864A form. Any discrepancy should be explained or corrected.

family-link.title: Supporting Family-Link Evidence
family-link.intro: Used when the household member's relationship is more distant or non-standard, to establish the household connection.

sections.title: When this applies
sections.body: For household members who are other relatives (aunt, uncle, cousin, non-relative household member), standard civil records like birth certificates may not directly show the link. Additional supporting evidence helps.

sections.title: What to include
sections.body:
• Family tree documentation or affidavit of relationship
  • Any relevant civil records showing the family connection
  • Shared address or financial co-dependence records

sections.title: Note
sections.body: For non-standard relationships, consulting an immigration attorney before relying on household member income is strongly recommended.
